function: Learns IRS phase shifts (four quadrant agents) and BS beamforming vectors (one agent) jointly with adaptive online MADDPG, maximizing a reward of rate, energy efficiency and latency (pp. 6-7).
system: BS with 64 antennas (8x8 UPA), 2-20 single-antenna IoT devices, reflecting IRS with 16-512 elements and 2-3 bit phase, 0.3 THz carrier, 10 GHz bandwidth (pp. 4, 12).
method: Multiagent deep reinforcement learning (MADDPG actor-critic, 3 hidden layers 256-128-64), centralized training with decentralized execution; online adaptation via change detection and multiresolution replay buffer (pp. 8-12).
data_channel: Custom THz channel with molecular absorption (Eqs. 1-5); path loss '3GPP Indoor THz with absorption'; Sionna simulation, 30 m x 30 m indoor; no dataset (pp. 4-5, 12).
test_conditions: Trained under stable conditions (Fig. 8); tested under abrupt mobility and absorption shifts every 5 s, humidity 20-80%, 0-30 km/h, 16-512 IRS elements, 2-20 users (pp. 13-15).
baselines: Non-learned: alternating optimization (AO), random phase shift (RPS). Learned: conventional MADDPG, single-agent DDPG, DQN (p. 12).
metrics: Sum rate, energy efficiency, end-to-end latency (average, 95th percentile, worst case), reliability, adaptation latency, recovery percentage, convergence episodes (pp. 13-15).
complexity: Per-iteration time O(N_IRS|M_i| + K N_T), space complexity Eq. 76; processing 1.2-6.8 ms, memory 245-1124 MB (Table V); linear scaling O(M+K) (pp. 11, 15).
q1_support: p. 12: Table II "Path Loss Model: 3GPP Indoor THz with absorption" and "THz channel models with molecular absorption dynamics using the Sionna library"; the channel is the custom model of Eqs. 1-5 (pp. 4-5); no TR 38.901 profile, dataset or measurement is named.
q2_support: p. 13: "We introduce three types of environmental shifts at 5-s intervals: 1) user mobility change; 2) absorption coefficient fluctuation; and 3) combined"; p. 15: "achieves 90% recovery within 5 ms" after training under stable conditions.
q3_support: p. 12: "We compare against five state-of-the-art approaches: 1) C-MADDPG; 2) single-agent DDPG (SA-DDPG); 3) deep Q-network (DQN); 4) alternating optimization (AO); and 5) random phase shift (RPS)"; p. 13: "18.1 Gb/s compared to 12.5 Gb/s for C-MADDPG and 9.8 Gb/s for AO".
q4_support: p. 11: "The per-iteration time complexity is O(NIRS · |Mi| + K · NT)" (Eq. 75); p. 15: Table V total processing time 1.2, 3.5 and 6.8 ms and "linear computational scaling (O(M + K))".
q5_support: p. 12: "We implement realistic THz channel models with molecular absorption dynamics using the Sionna library"; all channels are simulated and the paper gives no code link, DOI, public dataset or measured data.
notes: Area 3: the learned agents set IRS phases and BS beamformers (physical layer); frequency band and power level are only mentioned as discrete state-action components (p. 10). Reviewer to confirm q1: Table II and p. 12 mention 3GPP path loss and Sionna but no TR 38.901 profile, and Eqs. 1-5 define a custom channel. q2 rests on online adaptation after abrupt mobility and absorption shifts (Fig. 4, Table III), not on a separate test scenario. C-MADDPG is the proposed method without its adaptive modules, so only SA-DDPG and DQN count as learned baselines for q3. Tables II to V were read from the page images (pp. 12, 14, 15).
